bib.title: The Unreasonable Ineffectiveness of the Deeper Layers

question: How much of the depth of open-weight pretrained LLMs can be removed (and healed with light QLoRA finetuning) before question-answering performance and next-token loss degrade, and what does that say about where knowledge is stored?
hypothesis: Because of the residual structure, deeper layers whose output is similar to their input can be removed with little harm; shallow layers matter more (hypotheses 0-2 in Sec 3.1).
contributions: A layer-pruning method that picks the block of n consecutive layers with minimal angular distance between its input and output, then heals with QLoRA
A simpler heuristic: drop the deepest n layers before the final layer, then heal
Evidence that QA accuracy (MMLU, BoolQ) is flat until a model-dependent pruning fraction then collapses to random, while healed C4 loss rises smoothly
Evidence that GSM8K and HellaSwag degrade at any pruning, suggesting deeper layers matter for reasoning

method.summary: Compute angular distance between the final-token representation entering layer l and layer l+n on C4 validation samples, drop the n-layer block with the minimum distance, then heal with 4-bit QLoRA (FFN modules only) on C4 for 5000 steps at batch 16. Evaluate MMLU, BoolQ and C4 validation loss across pruning fractions for seven open-weight models.
method.task: post-training layer pruning of pretrained decoder-only LLMs, with PEFT healing

datasets.name: C4 (en, train split)
datasets.size: 164M tokens (7B and smaller) or 328M tokens (13B and larger) per healing run
datasets.preprocessing: long examples truncated to max seq length; special tokens added when available; Qwen needed a default padding token

datasets.name: C4 validation
datasets.size: 60k randomly sampled sequences, fixed across models

datasets.name: MMLU
datasets.split: cais/mmlu, dev set used for few-shot examples
datasets.preprocessing: original formatting, no prompt engineering; average accuracy over all subjects

training.lr: peak 3e-4 for most models; Phi-2 2e-4; Llama-2-70B 3e-5; Mistral-7B 3e-6
training.seeds: SEED_VAL = 0 via transformers.enable_full_determinism; finetuning seeds 0 to 2 ablated on Llama-2-13B (Fig 9)

other.lora_targets: FFN only: gate_proj/down_proj/up_proj (Llama, Mistral); fc1/fc2 (Phi-2); w1/w2/c_proj (Qwen)
other.lora_rank_protocol: start at 64; if healing clearly harms vs no healing, sweep ranks and pick best by MMLU; chosen on the simple heuristic (except Llama-2-70B)

inference.samples: GSM8K pass@1 from a single generation per problem; other evals single run
inference.prompting: MMLU 5-shot in main text (Sec 4.1, Fig 2); Appendix B.2 says 0 few-shot examples; BoolQ 0-shot; CoT-MMLU via flan_cot_fewshot

parameters.pruning_n: number of layers removed, varied up to ~80% of layers
parameters.angular_distance: d = (1/pi) arccos(x_l . x_{l+n} / (|x_l||x_{l+n}|)) on the final token T, averaged over samples
parameters.simple_heuristic: drop layers L-n to L-1, excluding the final layer

metrics.name: Normalized C4 validation loss
metrics.definition: cross-entropy divided by log V of the model vocab

metrics.name: GSM8K pass@1
metrics.definition: gsm8k_cot, one CoT generation per problem

eval.protocol: Single run per point, no significance tests; ablations on prompt order, few-shot count, finetuning seed, LoRA rank on Llama-2-13B/Mistral-7B/Llama-2-7B/70B.

availability.data: public Hugging Face datasets and checkpoints (Appendix B.1 table)

evidence.quote: For our experiments, we use 0 few-shot examples; our results and analysis are robust to this choice, cf. Figure 8.

results.claim: Layers to prune are chosen as the n-block with minimum angular distance between its input and output representations, then healed.
results.setup: all seven models; distance on final token, averaged over 10k C4 validation samples
results.quote: Find the layer, ℓ∗, that minimizes that distance:

results.claim: Healing uses 4-bit QLoRA on C4 for 5000 steps at global batch size 16.
results.setup: all models; LoRA dropout 0.05, FFN-only targets, cosine LR with 100 warmup steps
results.quote: Models were finetuned for 5000 steps with a global batch size of 16

results.claim: Healing token budget is 164M or 328M C4 tokens, on a single 40GB A100.
results.quote: on either 164M or 328M tokens from the Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus (C4)

results.claim: Llama-2 family MMLU accuracy transitions sharply to random at a pruning fraction around 45%-55%.
results.quote: a pruning fraction around 45%-55% for models in the Llama-2 family

results.claim: Mistral-7B MMLU transitions to random at about 35% pruning.
Phi-2 MMLU transitions to random at about 25% pruning.
Qwen family MMLU transitions to random at about 20% pruning (Qwen-7B, Qwen-14B).
results.quote: and 20% for models from the Qwen family

results.claim: The paper's stated overall range for the collapse to random guessing across models is 20%-55%.
results.setup: MMLU (Fig 2) and BoolQ (Fig 7) captions, all seven models
results.quote: performances are quite robust until 20%-55% pruning fractions, depending on model family and size
results.note: Abstract says only 'up to half'; Fig 1 caption gives 40%-50% for Llama-2-70B and Sec 1 says 'up to roughly half'.

results.claim: Llama-2-70B QA accuracy collapses between 40% and 50% pruning (Fig 1 caption).
results.quote: sharp transitions in performance for the accuracy of question-answering tasks (here between 40%-50% pruning fraction)

results.claim: Healed C4 loss increases smoothly with no transition through the pruning fractions where QA accuracy collapses.
results.setup: normalized C4 validation loss, healed, seven models
results.quote: continuity and very slow growth in the healed loss (light blue) up to at least to 80% pruning fraction

results.claim: Healing gives only modest MMLU gains and pushes the transition slightly later; the simple deepest-layers heuristic is much worse than similarity pruning without healing but nearly equal after healing.
results.quote: with healing, the scores of both methods are quite similar

results.claim: Authors conclude the purpose of healing is repairing the pruning interface, not acquiring knowledge.
results.quote: These experiments are strong evidence that the purpose of post-pruning finetuning is the healing of damage at the pruning interface and not the acquisition of additional knowledge.

results.claim: GSM8K and HellaSwag degrade immediately under any pruning, while CoT-MMLU stays flat like MMLU.
results.setup: Llama-2-70B, similarity-informed pruning (Fig 6); values only in figure
results.quote: both GSM8K and HellaSwag, our two reasoning tasks, exhibit immediate degradation in performance with any amount of pruning

results.claim: Unpruned Llama-2-70B CoT-MMLU is about 43% versus about 69% for MMLU without CoT.
Authors' interpretation: shallow layers likely store and retrieve knowledge, deeper layers support higher-level computation such as math reasoning.
results.setup: inference from MMLU/BoolQ vs GSM8K/HellaSwag results
results.quote: the shallow layers likely play a critical role in the storing of knowledge and retrieving of information, while the deeper layers are important for higher-level computations such as mathematical reasoning

results.claim: Layer pruning is more robust in larger, deeper models (Llama-2-13B, 70B).
results.quote: layer pruning is more robust for the larger and deeper models
results.note: Authors offer two untested explanations: smaller models more overtrained, or deeper models can lose more layers in absolute terms.

results.claim: Lower LoRA rank generally improves MMLU after healing but worsens C4 loss, suggesting overfitting to C4 at higher ranks.
results.quote: decreasing the LoRA rank generally improves performance

results.claim: Similarity-informed pruning outperforms random-layer and shallow-layer pruning on MMLU.
results.quote: The similarity-informed pruning strategy clearly outperforms these baselines.
results.note: Fig 11 title says Llama-7B; caption says Llama-2 7B.

limits: Only QA-style benchmarks (MMLU, BoolQ) show the flat region; GSM8K, HellaSwag and C4 loss degrade immediately, so 'half the layers' applies to knowledge QA only
Single run per point, no confidence intervals; seed ablation only on Llama-2-13B
LoRA rank and some learning rates chosen per model by sweeps on MMLU, which tunes to the eval; compute did not allow an exhaustive sweep
Only 7 models, 2.7B-70B, all base pretrained models and one healing set (C4); no instruct models
Healing data C4 is probably lower quality than the models' pretraining data; authors suspect overfitting with higher ranks
Qwen family behaves anomalously (transition at ~20%); unexplained
MMLU shot count inconsistent: 5-shot in Sec 4.1/Fig 2, 0 few-shot in Appendix B.2
No latency or memory measurement reported; no code release stated
Authors concede they do not know why healing removes the transition in loss but not in QA accuracy
